raw_recipe.headline: Quick Salmon Salad
raw_recipe.description: This salmon salad recipe is super quick to make with canned or leftover salmon, celery, dill, and green onion tossed in a creamy lemon dressing.
raw_recipe.name: Quick Salmon Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Combine salmon, green onions, celery, mayonnaise, and lemon juice in a bowl until well combined; season with dill and salt to taste.

review.reviewBody: I've made this recipe three times. The first time, I followed it exactly and did find it to be a bit salty. However, the underlying taste was still good.... Decided to try it a second time, but changed the amount of the Seasoned Salt to 1/2 tsp. Big difference! This time, I felt it was PERFECT!! Followed the change my third attempt and served it up for a baby shower buffet. It was the first to disappear and I had many ask for the recipe!! Definitely would recommend it.

This is a very good change of pace from the typical tuna salad. I used more mayo for moisture, the juice of one whole lemon, and less salt, about 1/2 teaspoon. For more flavor I added 1/2 teaspoon curry powder, 1/2 teaspoon Mrs. Dash Lemon Pepper, 1 clove caramelized garlic crushed, 2 jalapenos chopped, 1 tablespoon capers rinsed and drained, and fresh ground pepper to taste. Served on a bed of fresh spinach, splashed with balsamic vinaigrette.

Caution: this recipe can be salty. I took notice of one of the reviews who mentioned it was too salty and I left out the seasoned salt. Still, I found it salty to my taste, but tolerable. The canned salmon I used had 240mg of sodium for 1/4 cup of fish. This recipe is delicous but be careful.

This is a great base recipe, I seasoned to my taste so I didn't suffer from the "too much salt" issue some did. Old Bay seasoning worked great in this, and this salad was tasty in a sandwich, thank you for posting!

This was excellent. I made it with two cans worth of leftover salmon from last night with a just of touch of smoked salmon I needed to use up. The combo of green onions, celery and dill add just the right flavor. I used lime juice as that's what I had, and no salt due to the smoked salmon. Yummy. Thanks for sharing this one.
Very good. Used 1 tsp each lemon juice & dill and only a dash of salt. Used 1/8 cup each sour creme and mayo. Makes lots - try half recipe?

Excellent recipe! I used grilled salmon (45 minutes on a Traeger smoker at about 200 degrees), so it required more mayo because the smoked salmon was dryer than the canned (I used 1/2 C), used coarse sea salt but reduced it by about 90%, and I also added 1/2 cup of sweet pickle relish. Served it on Rustic Bakery’s Sourdough Flatbread crackers.

Very good and healthful. I reduced seasoned salt to 1/2 tsp and squeezed more lemon juice into the mix than recipe called for. Didn't have dill so used dried basil. Will add a little lemon zest next time. I look forward to making this often. Much more flavorful than tuna salad.
Very easy & very tasty, easily adaptable for personal taste (I cut back on the mayo)! Something I like to make when I am tired of tuna salad.
Great recipe! I made it to use up about half a pound of cold poached salmon from last night's dinner party, reducing the seasoning salt to 1/4 teaspoon.

This was delicious. After reading the reviews I omitted the salt and used lemon pepper instead of lemon juice. Everything else was as the recipe called for. It was not dry at all. We doubled the recipe so on the second serving we added avocado sliced tomato and smoked paprika. I served it on lightly toasted sourdough bread. We will keep this in rotation for a long time. And like everything else we let it sit in the fridge overnight for the flavors to meld. Yummy 👍🏻👍🏻 Thank You LILREDCV for this GREAT recipe. I’ve been making this recipe every week for over a year now. For personal preference I have changed it up a little. I have omitted the Celery , Salt and Dill. Personal preference. I added 1/2 t of Low Sodium Lemon Pepper, 1 t Lemon Juice not from Concentrate, 1t Cayenne Pepper, 1t Smoked Paprika and 1/4 c Diced Red Bell Pepper. As well as the rest of your ingredients. Except I swapped 0 Fat Greek Yogurt for the Mayo. I have served it by itself, in a green salad, on Sourdough as a Salmon Melt and even added Panko to it and made Salmon Burgers. This is a great recipe Thank You for sharing this with us. I am adding this review to my original from 8/4/24 so my original review will remain on record. Thanks again for sharing. LOVES2COOK.

Good recipe- I read reviews and reduced s-salt and added few shakes of Old Bay. I also add diced hard-boiled egg but that is just based on family tradition- the recipe is good as is! (Just add salt sparingly to your taste).
Delicious. Did use less seasoned salt than recipe called for. Really good and will make this again.
I added dark red kidney beans and rainbow pasta. Rainbow tomato garnish. Yummy
This was a very nice recipe for a simple dinner. Easy to scale down for a single serving.

This was nothing special. I don't understand the rave reviews. It was okay but not delicious. It lacked flavor and was rather bland overall. This could easily become disgusting if you eat too much of it in one sitting.

Made this exactly as written and the only thing I'd change is to use less than the called for amount of seasoning salt, as it was a touch salty. But that will depend on the type of canned salmon you use, some are saltier than others. I served over butter lettuce leaves for a quick lunch. We all love this.
Dill juice works well also from pickle jar. Used coisants instead of bread. Also good on rice crackers.
I added a little more plant based mayonnaise, I use vegan mayo.
